long_biography.plain_text:
Banking became Rami Rifaat El Nimer's principal career after studies in Switzerland and a master's in money and banking at Adelphi University. He completed exchange placements with banks in London and New York before joining Lebanon's financial sector. In 2000 an investor group acquired a controlling stake in First National Bank; he became chairman and later general manager. He also holds a substantial personal stake in the bank.

El Nimer's second public identity grew from collecting Palestinian, Ottoman and wider regional art. He opened Dar El-Nimer for Arts and Culture in Beirut as a nonprofit platform for exhibitions, research and public programming. Born in Nablus to a banking family, he uses the collection to preserve cultural memory rather than treating it only as a private asset. Banking remains his core commercial interest, while the foundation expresses a separate cultural and philanthropic commitment.
